findings.reason: the four uncovered ids do fail at head (run here: `tests/test_a_new_lift_replaces_the_standing_one.py::test_the_cli_reply_carries_replaces_in_its_lift_field`, `tests/test_budget.py::test_cli_preflight_exits_three_when_a_backend_is_held`, `tests/test_budget.py::test_cli_preflight_exits_zero_when_every_backend_is_clear` and `tests/test_codex_banked_reset.py::test_cli_budget_reset_round_trip`, all exit 10) and §38's Deliverable already requires the node to confirm each id at its own base, so the misattribution cannot send the node down a wrong path — the repair is to the citation's wording, not to the work.
findings.text: §38 says "A limit-reset node's base arm observed the failures on 2026-10-22 (run r-20261022T034717545596-an-announcement-names-who-it-cannot-reach, logs/base.suite.log at f990f8063)" and lists thirteen ids under that citation, but that arm ran an 18-file gate whose persisted list (`runs/r-20261022T034717545596-.../logs/gate2-files.txt`) holds `tests/test_crew_families_fold.py` and `tests/test_preflight_pace.py` only: `logs/base.suite.log` reports 15 failed / 478 passed and carries 9 of the 13 ids, together with 6 lane-change ids (§`test_a_lane_change_keeps_its_waivers.py` 2, `test_crew_lane_change.py` 4) that §38 does not mention, so a reader resolving the citation finds neither the whole list nor only it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §38's id list is anchored to a base arm whose gate file list (`logs/gate2-files.txt`, 18 files) never names `tests/test_a_new_lift_replaces_the_standing_one.py`, `tests/test_budget.py` or `tests/test_codex_banked_reset.py`, so four of the thirteen ids are attributed to a log that cannot contain them.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — "all thirteen ids pass at head, and every other case in the five files still passes" is measurable, and §38's two controls are both negative controls (a repaired test pointed back at its retired verb must fail with exit 10, and a monkeypatched field of a successor's answer must fail the test that pins it).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the cited log and the run's arms sit under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261022T034717545596-an-announcement-names-who-it-cannot-reach/logs/` on GPFS, and §38 requires its own logs under the run directory, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §38's prose names mechanisms and commits only; nothing in it carries a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into code, and its changed artifacts are test files.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold as written: the twelve ids that drive retired verbs do fail with exit 10 (independently reproduced for six of them at head `e208a0a0c`, including the whole `test_preflight_pace.py` group and the lift, budget and banked-reset files), and `test_each_budget_flag_gives_the_answer_the_old_verb_gave` fails on its payload diff `{'reset_count': 0, 'resets': []}` rather than on the exit code, matching the change `569ab36e2` introduced; the successors `crew budget --check/--lift/--reset` exist and accept the arguments the tests already pass, so the described mechanism produces the done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable (repoint the thirteen budget ids to the successors their tombstones name), with no product-code change and a single verdict available.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §38 declares no cross-section dependency and needs none; its only cross-section reference is §35 as precedent, its write-path files resolve, and `plan-section-depends-on` carries no entry for `s38`.
